prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Boundary: offshore/shore wind-farm O&M; excludes public grid/unrelated port operations. Aliases: Glassfin=Turbine Controller; Morrowick=Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern=Weather Service; Juniper Vale=SCADA Gateway; Thistle Crown=Maintenance Planning Engine; Amber Quay=Shore Control Room; Kestrel Bay=Crew Transfer Vessel; Sable Orchard=Fleet Dispatch Console; Mosslight=Warehouse System; Copper Finch=Metocean Buoy; Quiet Harbor=Cybersecurity Gateway; Blue Granite=Vessel AIS Receiver; Larkspur=Blade Inspection Drone; Redoubt=Work Permit Portal; Foxglove=Emergency Generator; Wildmere=Grid Interface Relay. Others: Pitch System/Converter Cabinet/Nacelle Condition Monitor/Rotor Brake Unit/Turbine Sensor Bus/Main Transformer/Export Cable Monitor/Spares Hub/Helideck/Daughter Craft/Service Operations Vessel. Flows: controller→Pitch Deviation Notice→gateway→work-package flags/Session Revocation Receipt/status/measurements; warehouse→Backorder Exception Slip→Storekeeper validates unavailable parts before rescheduling; Duty Planner→Transfer Manifest Addendum using Field Supervisor/planning-engine input; AIS→timestamps/Position Quality Flag→Marine Coordinator/dispatch; buoy→Wave Burst Record/seas/offline logs; weather→Squall Window Bulletin/forecasts; substation→Transformer Tap Snapshot on requested review. Condition monitor/sensor bus/cable monitor supply degradation/operating/cable evidence. Planning: Duty Planner verifies urgent technical basis/feasibility; safety-threatening/substantial-generation-loss faults outrank inspections; due-date/condition/value justify planned outages. Field Supervisor validates faults/offshore visits. Planner evaluates access,parts,competence,duration; schedules long-lead work early. Dispatch assigns approved vessels/crews after priority confirmation. Weather Analyst checks confidence; coordinator checks vessel/transit/site limits, maintains/distributes daily plans and coordinates changes with Vessel Master/teams. Weather Hold blocks mobilization beyond approved limits. Blade Specialist reviews drone imagery; unsafe flights suspend; physical inspection mandatory. Substation Operator confirms constraints. Permits: Requester submits scope/location/duration/team/equipment; planner/reviewers/HSE Officer/coordinator/master review; Authorizer requires controls/bounds; supervisor checks prestart; changes trigger reassessment/suspension; teams report completion/issues; portal readiness/release checks required. Electrical: transformer→cable→grid; segregated auxiliaries; automatic emergency start; acceptable voltage/frequency before transfer;

New part:
S269: The Duty Planner revises priorities when asset condition, access forecasts, or resource availability changes, and communicates the resulting plan to affected teams.
S270: Weather Service provides forecast conditions and confidence information for planned work areas and vessel routes.
S271: Metocean Buoy observations give the team a local reference for checking forecast trends and current sea state.
S272: Weather Analyst compares forecast data with recent observations before advising on the reliability of a work window.
S273: Forecast confidence is considered alongside the predicted conditions rather than treated as a substitute for operational limits.
S274: The Duty Planner checks that the expected conditions remain within the limits for the task, transfer method, and vessel.
S275: Low confidence near a limit leads to more conservative planning and a shorter review interval.
S276: A Weather Hold is applied when conditions are outside the approved limits or the available evidence is insufficient to support safe work.
S277: The Marine Coordinator reviews access options and vessel availability when a work window narrows.
S278: The Vessel Master receives the Transfer Manifest Addendum before departure.
S279: The Crew Transfer Vessel proceeds only when the Vessel Master considers the approach and transfer conditions acceptable.
S280: A forecast that improves does not by itself release a hold, because the team also checks current observations and the task-specific limits.
S281: The Service Operations Vessel may provide a more stable work platform, but its operating limits still govern whether work can proceed.
S282: Vessel Standby is used when transit or station keeping remains possible but personnel transfer or task execution is not justified.
S283: The Marine Coordinator reassesses the route when wind direction, wave conditions, or visibility changes materially.
S284: The Vessel Master can pause or abort an approach when observed conditions differ from the forecast or deteriorate during transit.
S285: Maintenance Planning Engine produces the Deferred Task Rationale when weather prevents a planned task from proceeding.
S286: The rationale supports later reprioritization without implying that the task is safe under the current conditions.
S287: Quiet Harbor blocks a route change when the required authorization is incomplete.
S288: Blue Granite provides vessel position information for review against the planned route and operating area.
S289: The team considers forecast uncertainty when deciding whether to commit crews, fuel, and vessel time to a remote work site.
S290: When conditions are changing rapidly, the Marine Coordinator seeks an updated forecast before confirming a departure or transfer plan.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
